notes.exploratory: Experiment 8 is an exploratory projection (paper Appendix J), not part of the frozen registered protocol.
notes.synthetic_anchors: Record lengths beyond 2026 have no realized price data; anchors are a synthetic weekly Saturday grid (pandas.date_range(..., freq='W-SAT')) using the same genesis-relative age-in-weeks formula as data_loader.build_weekly_series. end_year=2026 reproduces exp1/exp2's 820-anchor, q=6 setup exactly.
notes.calibration_null_subgrid: Calibration (and the achieved-power statistic's GridCache) uses every 16th member of the declared 1,216-model family (76 members), not the full family: building Sigma_theta for all 1,216 members at one record length alone measured ~90s at n_obs=820 and scales like n_obs^2 (n_obs reaches ~1,860 by 2046); doing this for 8 (record length x volatility scenario) cells would not fit the time budget. Use --full for the complete family.
notes.oracle_null_subgrid: The oracle bound uses a further-reduced subgrid, every 32th member (38 members): oracle_power_bound's cost is dominated by per-null covariance construction (same O(n_obs^2) cost as above), repeated independently for each of the 3 representative alternatives at each of the 8 cells. Use --full for the complete family.
notes.n_draws_power: 100 Monte-Carlo histories per (end_year, scenario, model) achieved-power estimate (reduced from a starting point of 150 to fit the time budget; --full uses config.DIAGNOSTICS_N_HISTORIES_PAPER).
notes.n_draws_oracle: 50 draws per Neyman-Pearson test inside the oracle search: oracle cost is dominated by per-null covariance construction, not n_draws (exp2.py's N_DRAWS_RUN note), so this stays small even in --full.
notes.seed_family: seeds = 20261101 + end_year (+100000 for the declining scenario); a new seed family for this experiment, distinct from config.S1_CALIBRATION_SEED (reserved for the primary registered test).
notes.representative_models: (a) random_walk_cycle_lam1: AR c=0 (random walk) + the representative cycle, lambda=1; (b) ar_c5_cycle_lam1: AR c=5 + the representative cycle, lambda=1; (c) random_walk_lam0: AR c=0, no cycle, lambda=0 (paper Section 5/Appendix J).

volatility_scenarios.flat: future annual volatility held at config.ANNUAL_VOLATILITY[2026].
volatility_scenarios.declining: OLS fit of log-volatility against year over 2017-2026 (not specified by the paper beyond 'declining at the past rate'), extrapolated forward and floored at 0.02.
volatility_scenarios.implementation: src.deviation_family.sigma_profile reads config.ANNUAL_VOLATILITY as a module global when no override is passed (which is how model_covariance/simulate_path/simulate_paths_batch call it); src/config.py and src/deviation_family.py may not be edited, so each scenario's extra years (2027..end_year) are added to config.ANNUAL_VOLATILITY in place for the duration of that cell's simulations only, saved and restored via try/finally immediately afterward. config.CALIBRATION_SUPPORT_YEARS (captured at import time from the original 2011-2026 keys) is untouched, so the volatility-shape RMS normalization stays fixed across every record length and scenario, matching its documented 'held fixed' design.

notes.b_grid: np.arange(0, 30+0.375, 0.75), 41 points, exactly as exp1.py's b_grid().
notes.plot: exp8_power_curves.png averages achieved power and the oracle bound over the 3 representative models at each (end_year, scenario), to show exactly one line per (scenario x bound-type) as requested.
